questions.prompt: In the cache-aside pattern, what happens on a cache miss?

options.text: The application reads from the database, stores the result in the cache, and returns it
The cache blocks all other reads

questions.explanation: On a miss, cache-aside reads the source (database), populates the cache, and returns the value, so subsequent reads hit the cache.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of write-back (write-behind) caching?

options.text: Data can be lost if the cache fails before flushing to the database
The cache can never be read

questions.explanation: Write-back acknowledges the write after updating the cache and flushes to the database later, so a cache failure before the flush loses data. The upside is fast writes.

questions.prompt: What does an LRU eviction policy evict when the cache is full?

options.text: The entry unused for the longest time

questions.explanation: LRU (Least Recently Used) drops the entry that has gone unused the longest, keeping recently accessed data available.

questions.prompt: A viral item's cache entry expires and thousands of requests miss at once, flooding the database. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Synchronized misses on a hot key create a cache stampede. Mitigate with TTL jitter, request coalescing, and serving slightly stale data during refresh.

questions.prompt: Which are valid ways to handle cache staleness? Select all that apply.

options.text: Set a TTL so entries expire
Explicitly invalidate the entry when the data changes
Use write-through to keep the cache fresh on every write
Never write to the database again

questions.explanation: TTLs, explicit invalidation, and write-through are the standard tools for bounding or eliminating staleness. Not writing to the database is not a real option.

questions.prompt: The fraction of reads served from the cache rather than the backing store is called the cache ______ ratio. (one word)
questions.explanation: The cache hit ratio measures how often reads are served from cache; a higher ratio means more latency and load saved.
